rules_evaluated.evidence: lines 99-103, new '## Pre-read before Module 4' section (per this file's own maintainer note dated 2026-07-30: 'first pre-read section in this file... re-audit before ship'): 'Read: Simon Willison, Designing agentic loops (September 2025). The skill Willison names is choosing what the agent can iterate against before you start it: the tools it can run, the checks that tell it how it's doing, the room to fail safely. Module 4 opens on a run you send off and step away from; this is the thinking you do before stepping away.' This names exactly the elements of Ronacher's three-pattern (tools/reference artifact, checks/external verifier, safe iteration room) that the strategy doc reserves for M5: 'M5 teaches packaging by diagnosing M4's failures... what Ronacher's three-pattern (reference artifact + plan.md + external verifier) actually adds.' M4's own strategy-doc detail is explicit the send-off must stay un-packaged by design: 'No plan.md, no verifier, no reference artifact — just "here's my system, go do X."' and 'The task must be hard enough that an un-packaged run will be "not great"... If the task is simple enough to succeed un-packaged, it's the wrong task.' Priming students, in the gap right before M4, to think in terms of checks/verifier/safe-fail-room risks softening M4's deliberately unpackaged failure — the exact contrast M5 is built to diagnose. This pre-read is not named or blessed anywhere in the strategy doc (grep for 'Designing agentic loops' / this Willison piece in content-strategy-agentic-engineering-101.md returns no hit).
